Thursday Nov 12, 08:47–12:27 UTC (3h40), a SEV2: customer dashboards showed stale data [1].

**What broke:** deploy of ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB; with the 512 Mi memory limit, ingest-worker pods OOM'd on the first large batch and crash-looped — and the change went to all pods at once [1]. Detection was slow: no consumer-lag alert, first signal was a Sentry OOM alert at 09:14, 27 min after deploy [1]. Rolled back to v2.13.3 at 10:05, lag drained by 12:27 [1].

**Customer data:** none lost. Events kept arriving in Kafka and were processed late; Lior's reconciliation on Nov 13 confirmed per-workspace event counts match Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC [1][4]. All workspaces had delayed dashboards; 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts) [1].

**Changes so it doesn't happen again:**
- KES-431: page the on-call when consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1]
- KES-432: ingest config changes go to the canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1]
- KES-433: raise worker memory to 1 Gi + load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1]
- Merged Nov 13: ingest#419 reverted the default to 1 MB and added a guard refusing batches >25% of the container memory limit [8]

Note: Orbitly has claimed an SLA service credit under section 7 of their MSA, with Sam handling it in the renewal [3][7].
